summary: Turns the search page into a client component that reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and lists them.

findings.title: URL query rendered as raw HTML
findings.description: The heading injects the q URL parameter into the page as raw HTML. Nothing sanitizes or escapes the query first. An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS. Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.
findings.problem: The heading injects the q URL parameter into the page as raw HTML. Nothing sanitizes or escapes the query first.
findings.consequence: An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect without dependency array refetches forever
findings.description: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each fetch calls setResults with a new array, which triggers another render. The page sends search requests to the catalog API in an endless loop. This wastes client and server resources. Pass [query] as the dependency array so the effect runs only when the query changes.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.description: SearchPage returns early when q is empty, before it calls useState and useEffect. The number of hooks then changes between renders. React throws a hooks mismatch error when q goes from empty to non-empty on client navigation. The page crashes. Call useState and useEffect before any early return. Skip the fetch inside the effect when query is empty.

findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before any early return. Skip the fetch inside the effect when query is empty.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.description: The change deletes the form and input that let users enter a search term. The page now asks users to type a term but offers no input. Users who open the search page without q have no way to search. Keep the search form on the page, both in the empty state and above the results.

findings.title: Search failure not handled
findings.description: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok, but the promise chain has no catch. The rejection goes unhandled. Users see an empty list with no error message when the search fails. The rejection also logs as unhandled. Add a catch handler that records an error state and render a message for it.

findings.title: List items rendered without a key
findings.description: Each li built from results has no key prop. Product already has a stable id field. React logs a key warning and cannot reconcile the list efficiently when results change. Set key to product.id on each li.
